title: What Happens When Earth's Magnetic Field Flips?
description:
What Happens When Earth's Magnetic Field Flips?

Earth's north magnetic pole is racing across the Arctic towards Siberia, and one day north and south will swap places. Life has survived hundreds of magnetic flips — so why do satellites already have to shut down over the South Atlantic, how do we know Earth's compass can turn upside down, and what will the night sky look like when the poles trade places?

Sources: NASA Science, Flip Flop: Why Variations in Earth's Magnetic Field Aren't Causing Today's Climate Change — pole motion and past reversals (https://science.nasa.gov/science-research/earth-science/flip-flop-why-variations-in-earths-magnetic-field-arent-causing-todays-climate-change/) · British Geological Survey, Reversals — the liquid outer core and atmospheric shielding (https://geomag.bgs.ac.uk/education/reversals.html) · NASA (2020), NASA Researchers Track Slowly Splitting 'Dent' in Earth's Magnetic Field — the South Atlantic Anomaly and spacecraft radiation (https://www.nasa.gov/missions/station/nasa-researchers-track-slowly-splitting-dent-in-earths-magnetic-field/).

Pictures: NASA/GSFC Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS 3822, SVS 12312, SVS 20297) and NASA/ISS Crew Earth Observations (ISS030-E-078095 and HDEV) alongside original animated explainers, with AI-assisted voice and editing. Facts: every number is checked against the sources listed above.
Image credits: NASA/GSFC Scientific Visualization Studio (Greg Shirah, Tom Bridgman, Michael Starobin, Bailee DesRocher, Genna Duberstein, Eric Christian, Kayvon Sharghi, Joycelyn Thomson Jones, Jay Herman, Adam Szabo, Alexander Marshak); NASA/ISS Crew Earth Observations and Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit, Johnson Space Center.
